title: The Oldest Complaint Letter in the World
notes: Register: funny first, then land the point. Brisker than the previous videos. The comedy is in understatement and timing: the animation can be playful, but never mugs for the joke.
Shorter than the others, roughly 16 to 17 minutes. That is deliberate: the story is lighter and padding would hurt it.

The real complaint tablet appears as a photo card many times, from several photographers. The isolated PNG (p03) sits on the dark display ground as a card. Generated clay tablets are always blank or seen edge-on: never with wedge marks that could pass for a real text.
The tablet's text is paraphrased throughout the narration. No published translation is quoted, on screen or in audio. On-screen words are short paraphrase only, never presented as a translation.
p02 and p13 are real cuneiform tablets that are NOT Ea-nasir's. Their captions say so and must be shown.
Copper ingots are drawn as plano-convex 'bun' ingots, flat on one face and domed on the other. Never the Mediterranean four-handled oxhide shape: wrong region and period.
Nothing from the royal cemetery is drawn. The spectacular finds appear only through the photograph of the silver lyre (p15).
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API.
Guide object: the clay tablet itself, which opens, recurs and closes the film.

nanni.desc: Nanni, a merchant of Ur around 1750 BC: fringed wool robe over one shoulder, sandals, a short beard as a simple shape, simple vague face, very expressive posture

ea_nasir.desc: Ea-nasir, a copper merchant of Ur around 1750 BC: a richer fringed robe, a cap, a big leather purse, simple vague face, relaxed shrugging posture

messenger.desc: Gimil-Sin, Nanni's agent and messenger, a lean young man of Ur in a short tunic with a satchel, simple vague face

scribe.desc: a scribe of Ur around 1750 BC, sitting cross-legged with a reed stylus and a clay slab, simple vague face

woolley.desc: Leonard Woolley, an archaeologist of the 1920s in a pith helmet, shirt sleeves and shorts, simple vague face

crowd.desc: extras: townspeople of Ur around 1750 BC, a weary letter writer, 1920s excavation workers with baskets, a 2015 museum visitor seen from behind, simple vague faces

sets.desert_track: an empty dirt track across a dry open plain toward low hills, heat haze
